name: E-mail
tagline: An SMTP server and a SendGrid v3 API that catch every message, extract codes and links, and play the recipient.

capabilities.title: Every message, kept
capabilities.text: HTML, text, headers and attachments of every message, filtered by recipient, subject, kind, language or inbox.

capabilities.title: Codes and links extracted
capabilities.text: Built-in code, links and attachments extractors, plus your own regex, CSS selector or header rules.

capabilities.title: Inboxes that decide
capabilities.text: An inbox accepts, bounces, defers N times, holds or drops what lands in it; temporary inboxes expire by themselves.

capabilities.title: Steps after delivery
capabilities.text: Inbox steps open the message or click a link after a wait, with jitter, so tests never wait for a person.

capabilities.title: Act as the recipient
capabilities.text: Open, click, spam report or unsubscribe sends SendGrid's Event Webhook, signed with ECDSA, to your app.

capabilities.title: Hold and decide
capabilities.text: A held message waits for you: deliver, defer, bounce hard or soft, or drop; the app gets the matching event.

capabilities.title: Strict or unreachable intake
capabilities.text: Validate keys (401, or 535 on SMTP), drop STARTTLS, refuse recipients with 550 or 451, or time out.

capabilities.title: Wait, or expect none
capabilities.text: wait_for_message returns the extracted value; expect_no_message passes only if nothing arrives in time.

excerpts.title: The message, and what was pulled out of it

callouts.title: Temporary inbox
callouts.text: A test made this address; it expires by itself in 18 min.

callouts.title: How it came in
callouts.text: Via the SendGrid API or SMTP, with sender, recipient, time and trace.

callouts.title: Extracted code
callouts.text: Your extractor found the OTP; wait_for_message with extract returns it.

callouts.title: Links
callouts.text: Every link is detected; short links can be followed to the final URL.

callouts.title: Events
callouts.text: Delivery and recipient events sent to the app's Event Webhook.

excerpts.title: An inbox decides what happens on arrival

callouts.title: Temporary
callouts.text: Made by a test over the API; extend it or keep it with the environment.

callouts.title: Bounce it
callouts.text: Hard bounce, 550 mailbox unavailable, as the provider's event.

callouts.title: Defer N times
callouts.text: Defer 3 times, then accept: tests the app's retry.

callouts.title: Hold it
callouts.text: Decide by hand with decide_held, or let the steps decide.

callouts.title: Automatic steps
callouts.text: Delivered, opened 30 s later with 5 s of jitter, click signLink: no person needed.

callouts.title: Take it from
callouts.text: Subject, text, HTML, link, header or attachment.

callouts.title: Rule
callouts.text: A regex, CSS selector or header name; a capture group becomes the value.

callouts.title: Follow redirects
callouts.text: For short links: the value is the final URL.

callouts.title: Against the last 50
callouts.text: test_extractor runs the rule on recent mail: matched, skipped, no such link.

callouts.title: Why not
callouts.text: Messages where the rule found nothing, with the reason and a suggested fix.

provoke.name: Bounce
provoke.what: Hard or soft; the app gets the bounce event

provoke.name: Defer, then accept
provoke.what: The message is deferred N times before delivery

provoke.name: Dropped
provoke.what: The provider refuses to send it

provoke.name: Spam report
provoke.what: The recipient marks it as spam; signed event to the app

provoke.name: Unsubscribe
provoke.what: The recipient unsubscribes; signed event to the app

provoke.name: Provider unreachable
provoke.what: The intake times out, refuses, or answers 503 or 429

provoke.name: TLS trouble
provoke.what: SMTP without STARTTLS, or a TLS failure

provoke.name: Recipients refused
provoke.what: SMTP answers 550 or 451 to RCPT TO

provoke.name: Revoked key
provoke.what: Sends get 401, or 535 on SMTP, while keys are validated

advantages.title: Nothing leaves the machine
advantages.text: Mail to any domain is caught and never reaches a real inbox, so tests can use any address.

advantages.title: Bounces on demand
advantages.text: Hard and soft bounces, defers and drops happen when the test asks, not when a real server feels like it.

advantages.title: Values, not HTML scraping
advantages.text: Tests ask for extract=otp or a link and get the value; the extractor shows why a message did not match.

advantages.title: Throwaway inboxes
advantages.text: Each test makes its own inbox that expires on its own, so parallel runs never read each other's mail.

agent.prompt: Test the password reset e-mail end to end and get me the reset link.
tools: Messages with filters, or grouped by kind
Headers, text, HTML, extracted values, events
Wait for a message; with extract, return the value
Pass only if nothing arrives in time
A temporary or kept inbox with its rule and steps
Deliver, defer, bounce or drop a held message
Open, click, spam report or unsubscribe
Run a rule on one message or the last N
Make the intake strict or unreachable

notes: SMTP uses a self-signed certificate for STARTTLS; SendGrid is served on 8025.
Extractors live in email/extractors.yaml and also work for SMS.
